note: 21 hook formulas, with examples in Design Industries' world: Atlassian, AI in the enterprise, licensing, Cloud migration, a 25-person Melbourne team. Line 1 of a LinkedIn post is the whole game - the feed truncates at roughly 210 characters on desktop and 140 on mobile before 'see more', so the hook has to survive alone. Every formula here has a template, a filled example, what it is for, and the way it usually gets ruined. The examples are illustrations of shape, not facts to reuse: every number in a real post has to be DI's own.
rules: One idea per hook. If it needs a comma splice, it needs two posts.
Line 2 is not a hook, it is the payoff of line 1. Never waste it on setup.
No question marks in line 1 unless the question is specific enough that only DI could ask it.
Numbers beat adjectives. '$42,000 in unused licences' beats 'a lot of waste' every time.
If the hook works with any other partner's name on it, it is not DI's hook.
Australian English. No em dash, anywhere, ever.
Clients are anonymous unless the receipt records approval for that post.

hooks.name: Contrarian Take
hooks.template: Everyone says {common advice}. After {specific experience}, I think that is wrong.
hooks.example: Everyone says run the AI pilot for a quarter. We ran month-long ones for a year and every quarter-long pilot I saw was a delay with a budget code.
hooks.best_for: Establishing a point of view. Highest comment rate of any formula. Michael's natural formula.
hooks.trap: Being contrarian about something nobody believes. The belief has to be genuinely common in Australian enterprise IT.

hooks.name: Number Reveal
hooks.template: I {did thing} for {N} {days/weeks}. Here is what actually happened.
hooks.example: We ran licence audits on 30 Atlassian estates in 12 months. 26 were paying for seats nobody had logged into since the year before.
hooks.best_for: Experiments, audits, anything with a countable result across engagements.
hooks.trap: Burying the number. Put it in line 1 or the formula does nothing.

hooks.name: Mistake Confession
hooks.template: {Specific cost} is what {one mistake} cost me.
hooks.example: $18,000 is what one unread renewal notice cost a client of ours in March. We should have caught it.
hooks.best_for: Trust. People forward the posts where you look bad. Works for DI because most partners never admit one.
hooks.trap: A fake-humble mistake. 'We care too much about quality' reads as a brag and kills the post.

hooks.name: Before / After
hooks.template: {Time ago} I was {low state}. Today I {high state}. The difference was {one thing}.
hooks.example: 18 months ago our service desk answered tier-1 tickets by hand. Today Rovo answers the first 40 a day. One agent did it.
hooks.best_for: Proof DI has travelled the distance the reader wants to travel.
hooks.trap: Three-part transformations. Name one lever or the reader stops believing you.

hooks.name: The List Promise
hooks.template: {N} things I wish someone had told me before {milestone}.
hooks.example: 7 things I wish someone had told me before our first Data Center to Cloud migration.
hooks.best_for: Saves. Highest save rate of the 21, which LinkedIn weights heavily. Natural DI page post.
hooks.trap: N above 10. The reader does not believe you have 15 good ones, and you do not.

hooks.name: Insider Secret
hooks.template: After {N} years {doing thing}, here is the part nobody puts in the {job posting/course/pitch}.
hooks.example: After 25 years delivering Atlassian, here is the part nobody puts in the migration proposal.
hooks.best_for: Credentialed takes. Works only if the years are real, and DI's are.
hooks.trap: Promising a secret and delivering common knowledge. The admins in the comments will say so.

hooks.name: The Callout
hooks.template: If you are still {doing outdated thing}, stop.
hooks.example: If you are still buying Atlassian licences on the renewal notice without a last-login report, stop.
hooks.best_for: Short posts with one instruction. Fastest to write of the 21.
hooks.trap: Calling out something nobody does. Or worse, calling out your own audience with contempt.

hooks.name: Question Trap
hooks.template: {Specific scenario with a real cost}. What do you do?
hooks.example: Your Atlassian renewal lands Friday, it is 30% up on last year, and the CFO wants it 10% down. Six days. What do you do?
hooks.best_for: Comment volume. People answer scenarios, they ignore 'thoughts?'.
hooks.trap: A question with an obvious right answer. There has to be a real fork.

hooks.name: Story Cold Open
hooks.template: "{Line of dialogue}"\n\n{Who said it, when, and why it mattered}.
hooks.example: "Can we just add 200 more licences and sort it out later?"\n\nThat was the CIO of a listed group, on a Thursday, and later cost them $140,000.
hooks.best_for: Long-form storytelling posts. Highest dwell time. Michael's second-best formula.
hooks.trap: Dialogue nobody would actually say. Use the real line, including the ugly parts, with the client anonymised.

hooks.name: The Receipt
hooks.template: {Screenshot or hard number}. {One sentence of context}.
hooks.example: 4,000 seats, 11 months, zero weekend cutovers. Here is the migration plan that did it.
hooks.best_for: Anything DI can prove. Pair with a Tejas tile and reach roughly doubles.
hooks.trap: A receipt with no story attached. The number opens the door, the story is the room.

hooks.name: Myth Bust
hooks.template: {Popular explanation} is not why {bad outcome} is happening to you.
hooks.example: Atlassian's pricing is not why your renewal went up 30%.
hooks.best_for: Reframing. Sets you up to deliver the real cause in line 3.
hooks.trap: Busting the myth and never naming the replacement. Always name it.

hooks.name: The Comparison
hooks.template: {Expensive option} vs {cheap option}. {Surprising verdict}.
hooks.example: A $300,000 ITSM platform vs Jira Service Management and a fortnight of configuration. The fortnight won.
hooks.best_for: Tool and process posts. Very high share rate.
hooks.trap: An unfair comparison. Concede what the expensive option genuinely does better, and never name a competitor.

hooks.name: Permission Slip
hooks.template: You are allowed to {thing the reader feels guilty about}.
hooks.example: You are allowed to switch off the Marketplace apps nobody has opened since 2023.
hooks.best_for: Reach beyond the niche. These travel further than tactical posts.
hooks.trap: Generic self-care. It has to be specific to the working life of an Atlassian platform owner.

hooks.name: Pattern Interrupt
hooks.template: {One word or three-word line, full stop.}
hooks.example: We lost the tender.
hooks.best_for: Stopping the scroll cold. Whitespace does the work.
hooks.trap: Overuse. Once a month. Every post starting this way reads as a tic.

hooks.name: The Warning
hooks.template: {Common practice} is quietly costing you {specific thing they care about}.
hooks.example: Your 'temporary' second Jira instance is quietly costing you a migration you have not budgeted for.
hooks.best_for: Problem-aware audiences who have not connected cause to cost.
hooks.trap: Fear with no exit. Give the fix in the same post or you have just made a platform owner anxious.

hooks.name: Good vs Great
hooks.template: Good {role} {do X}. Great {role} {do Y}.
hooks.example: Good Atlassian admins answer the ticket. Great Atlassian admins write the automation rule so the ticket never arrives.
hooks.best_for: Quotable one-liners. Screenshot bait. Natural DI page post.
hooks.trap: A distinction that is really just 'try harder'. Y has to be a different action, not more effort.

hooks.name: Time Anchor
hooks.template: {Task} used to take me {long time}. It now takes {short time}.
hooks.example: A licensing proposal used to take us 5 hours. It now takes 20 minutes.
hooks.best_for: Tool, system and automation posts. The strongest hook shape for a how-to, and for anything DI AI Foundry ships.
hooks.trap: An unbelievable ratio. 5 hours to 20 minutes lands. 5 hours to 8 seconds does not.

hooks.name: The Unpopular Rule
hooks.template: I do not {widely accepted practice}. Ever. Here is why.
hooks.example: We do not let a client enquiry go unanswered overnight. Ever. We call it the Sundown Rule.
hooks.best_for: Positioning. Attracts the right clients by repelling the wrong ones. Explain the DI term in the same post.
hooks.trap: A rule you break constantly. Someone in the comments will know.

hooks.name: Curiosity Gap
hooks.template: The {superlative} {thing} I ever {verb} {broke the obvious rule}.
hooks.example: The best Cloud migration we ever ran started by deleting a third of the projects.
hooks.best_for: Openers that force the 'see more' tap.
hooks.trap: A gap you never close. Pay it off by line 4 or you have written clickbait.

hooks.name: The Walk-Away
hooks.template: I {fired/quit/deleted/cancelled} {valuable thing}. {Result}.
hooks.example: We turned down a 2,000-seat migration in January. The client came back in June with the budget to do it properly.
hooks.best_for: Values posts with a business result attached. Very high engagement.
hooks.trap: Walking away with no cost. Name what it actually cost DI or it reads as theatre.

hooks.name: The Direct Value
hooks.template: Here is the exact {artifact} I used to {specific outcome}. Steal it.
hooks.example: Here is the exact 4-question form we use before every AI Fast Start. Steal it.
hooks.best_for: Lead magnets and comment-for-link posts. Highest conversion of the 21. Natural DI page teach post.
hooks.trap: Making them ask for something you could have just posted. Give the artefact away in the post.
